key_insight: Dialogue re-cinematography turns a single wide-angle recording into multiple camera views. The paper explores grounding shot synthesis in audio to address lip-motion errors when the original video provides weak visual cues.
problem_solved: Filming close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder views is costly. Generating these views from one recording is an alternative, but visual-only generators struggle with speech-aligned lip motion when actors’ mouths are barely visible.
method: Use a single wide-angle dialogue video as the source for additional shots.
Ground shot synthesis in dialogue audio rather than relying on visual cues alone.
Target alternative framings with speech-consistent mouth motion; implementation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: This approach could reduce the need for multi-camera dialogue coverage and help practitioners build speech-aware video generation tools. The provided abstract is incomplete, so specific performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: One wide-angle source frame branching into close-up, medium, and over-the-shoulder views.
Audio waveform and video frames converging into a shot-generation model.
Illustration of a small, hard-to-see mouth in the source versus a prominent mouth in a generated close-up.
Speech waveform aligned with a sequence of mouth poses to explain audio–visual synchronization.
paper_title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
paper_authors: Anthony Chen, Naomi Ken Korem, Matan Ben-Yosef, Tavi Halperin, Urska Jelercic
